findings.title: Light/dark lightness values swapped in embedded-post author link
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss line 291, .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The light-theme branch should have stayed at 30% and the dark-theme branch should be 70% (100-30), per every other conversion in the PR. Consequence: on the default light theme the link changes from dark grey to very light grey and becomes low-contrast/unreadable on a light background, while on a dark theme it uses 30% instead of 70% and is too dark on a dark background.

findings.title: Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on desktop
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss line 522, .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The light value should have stayed 30% with dark value 70%. Consequence: light theme gets lighter than before, and .name becomes identical to .title below it (both 50%/50%), destroying the intended name/title hierarchy; dark theme gets 50% instead of 70% and is too dark.

findings.title: Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on mobile
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss line 497, .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Same error as desktop: light branch should remain 30% and dark branch should be 70%. Consequence: light-theme regression and loss of distinction versus .title, plus too-dark text on dark themes.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% on mobile
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). It should have become 20% for light and 80% for dark. Consequence: on light theme the heading becomes much lighter and indistinguishable from .topic-map h4 (which is correctly 50%/50%), losing heading hierarchy and contrast; on dark theme it uses 50% instead of 80% and is too dark.

findings.title: Light/dark values inverted in mobile custom-message-length
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss line 102, .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The branches are swapped: it should be 70% for light and 30% for dark, as correctly done for the same selector in desktop/modal.scss. Consequence: light theme becomes much darker than before and dark theme becomes much lighter/washed out, and mobile is inconsistent with desktop for the same class.

findings.title: Missed dark-theme conversion for category badge notification
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss line 115, .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still uses bare scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while every other 50% muted text in the same file was wrapped as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Consequence: the PR's dark-theme fix is incomplete; on a dark theme where $primary is light, lightening $primary yields near-white instead of the intended mid-grey from $secondary, so this count stays too bright/inconsistent with surrounding muted text.
